correctness.rationale: The append-letter recurrence F_{wc}(u)=F_w(u)+1_{u=vc}F_w(v) exactly partitions scattered-subsequence occurrence choices, so all 2^n binary words for n=2..14 and all their nonzero subwords are exhaustively handled by finite integer dynamic programming. The inspected verify.py explicitly loops product(01,repeat=n) for each n, checks no n≤13 exception and exactly four n=14 strings, confirms unique maximizers. The word 01010001110101 has unique most frequent subword 01001101 (length 8) with 144 occurrences versus maximum 136 for lengths≤7, directly refuting the half-length conjecture. Independent binary exhaustive recomputation for every word n≤14 and independent mask recomputation on two witnesses corroborated the source; computation is finite *exhaustive*, not an extrapolation to n>14.
